context.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloguing, circulation, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It guarantees strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons (Students, Public)
* Librarians / Circulation Staff
* Library Administrators
* Library Management System (Core System)
* External Identity Provider (SSO)
* External Payment Gateway
* Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Network

## Relationships
* Patrons and Staff interact with the Library Management System via HTTPS using TLS 1.3 and OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect.
* Core System integrates with external Payment Gateways and SSO Providers using automated secrets management within the EU perimeter.
* Core System connects to the Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Network using mutual TLS (mTLS), API signature validation, and circuit breakers.

## Technology Stack
* Hosting Infrastructure: EU-Central AWS/Azure regions provisioned via Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for repeatable deployments.
* Security & Auth: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect for authentication; AES-256 for data at rest; EU-hosted Key Management Service (KMS).
* Observability & Monitoring: Centralized APM strategy to track 99th-percentile search performance (<800ms) and SIEM integration for audit logging.

## Rationale
This architecture enforces strict regional boundaries and robust data protection to ensure full GDPR compliance for EU public and academic sectors. Circuit breakers, TLS 1.3, and automated secrets management protect system performance and security against external dependencies.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons, Librarians, Library Administrators
* External Identity Provider (SSO), External Payment Gateway, Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Network
* Self-Service Portal Container
* Staff Dashboard Container
* Notification Container
* Analytics/Reporting Container
* EU-hosted Kubernetes Clusters, Service Mesh, KMS/HSM

## Relationships
* Patrons to Self-Service Portal via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
* Self-Service Portal and Staff Dashboard to External Payment Gateway via HTTPS
* Internal containers communication via mTLS (Service Mesh / SPIFFE/SPIRE)
* Notification Container to external SMS/email providers via egress-controlled HTTPS

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes: Dedicated EU-central namespaces for data residency enforcement
* Service Mesh: mTLS and deny-by-default network policies for container isolation
* OAuth2/OIDC & JWT: Authentication and session management terminated at API Gateway
* KMS/HSM: EU-hosted envelope encryption for data at rest
* Message Broker: Durable queue (Kafka/SQS) for notification backpressure management

## Rationale
The architecture strictly enforces EU-only data residency via isolated Kubernetes infrastructure and egress controls. Dedicated resource pools and decoupled containers guarantee the sub-800ms search SLA.

Self-Service Portal Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System provides cataloging, circulation management, and self-service portals for public and academic libraries. It ensures strict EU-only data residency and high-performance search capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Library Patrons
- Self-Service Portal Container (Kubernetes, EU-hosted)
- External Identity Provider (SSO)
- External Payment Gateway
- Notification Container
- Analytics/Reporting Container

## Relationships
- Library Patrons -> Self-Service Portal Container: Accesses self-service portal [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- Self-Service Portal Container -> External Identity Provider: Authenticates patrons [OIDC with PKCE]
- Self-Service Portal Container -> External Payment Gateway: Processes fines [HTTPS]
- Self-Service Portal Container -> Notification Container: Triggers notifications [mTLS (Service Mesh / SPIFFE/SPIRE)]
- Self-Service Portal Container -> Analytics/Reporting Container: Sends usage metrics [mTLS (Service Mesh / SPIFFE/SPIRE)]

## Technology Stack
- Kubernetes: Hosts containerized services with Horizontal Pod Autoscaling for bursty search traffic.
- Envoy: Implements ingress-level rate limiting and DDoS protection.
- OpenTelemetry: Provides distributed tracing across services.
- AES-256: Secures data at rest for local persistent volumes and caches.
- TLS 1.3: Secures inbound patron traffic.

## Rationale
Decoupling search components within Kubernetes ensures sub-800ms search response times under heavy loads. Offloading payment processing to an external gateway minimizes PCI-DSS scope while maintaining strict EU data residency compliance.

Staff Dashboard Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The Staff Dashboard Container provides library staff and administrators secure, low-latency interfaces for circulation management, cataloging, and operational monitoring. It ensures strict EU data residency while maintaining high performance and strict audit compliance.]

## Key Elements
* Librarians & Library Administrators
* Staff Dashboard Container (Kubernetes, EU-hosted)
* Notification Container (Kubernetes, Kafka/SQS, EU-hosted)
* External Payment Gateway
* Interlibrary Loan (ILL) Network
* WORM Storage Sink
* Fluentbit Sidecar

## Relationships
* Librarians -> Staff Dashboard Container: Manages library operations [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
* Library Administrators -> Staff Dashboard Container: Configures and administers system [HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
* Staff Dashboard Container -> External Payment Gateway: Processes financial transactions with circuit breaker [HTTPS, strict egress]
* Staff Dashboard Container -> Notification Container: Triggers notifications [mTLS via SPIFFE/SPIRE]
* Staff Dashboard Container -> Kafka/SQS: Asynchronous batch processing [TLS]
* Fluentbit Sidecar -> WORM Storage Sink: Streams immutable audit logs [Encrypted TCP]

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes: Container orchestration for horizontal auto-scaling (HPA) and resource isolation
* Kafka / SQS: Message broker for asynchronous batch processing and decoupled queuing
* OpenTelemetry: Distributed tracing across external payment and notification services
* Fluentbit: Sidecar log shipping for immutable WORM audit trails
* DPoP (Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession): Cryptographic token binding for secure staff sessions
* Vault: Ephemeral runtime secret management for API keys

## Rationale
[This architecture balances high-throughput operational requirements with strict EU data residency and PCI-DSS security constraints. Asynchronous processing and circuit breakers protect backend stability while maintaining cryptographic audit immutability.]

Notification Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Library Management System is a public and academic solution designed to catalogue items, manage circulation, and provide self-service portals with strict EU data residency. The Notification Container asynchronously manages backpressure, multi-channel preferences, and dispatches alerts for patrons and staff.

## Key Elements
* Library Patrons & Staff
* Self-Service Portal Container & Staff Dashboard Container
* Notification Container (Kubernetes, Kafka/SQS, EU-hosted)
* Internal Preference Database (AES-256 encrypted, EU-restricted)
* External SMS/Email Providers

## Relationships
* Self-Service Portal Container -> Notification Container: Triggers notifications [mTLS (Service Mesh / SPIFFE/SPIRE)]
* Staff Dashboard Container -> Notification Container: Triggers notifications and requests retries [mTLS, JWT]
* Notification Container -> External SMS/Email Providers: Dispatches sanitized messages [Egress-controlled HTTPS, TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
* Kubernetes: Container orchestration for isolated, scalable deployment within EU boundaries
* Apache Kafka / AWS SQS: Asynchronous messaging queue to decouple workloads, manage backpressure, and implement DLQs
* AES-256: Encryption at rest for PII in Kafka/SQS and the preference database
* Prometheus & Grafana: Secure metrics export for delivery tracking without direct database queries
* SPIFFE/SPIRE & mTLS: Service mesh security for inter-container authentication

## Rationale
This architecture decouples notification workloads using Kafka/SQS to prevent cascading failures and maintain high search performance. Strict EU residency, AES-256 encryption, PII masking, and RBAC-gated APIs satisfy GDPR compliance and data protection mandates.

Analytics/Reporting Container.analysis:
## Overview
• Analytics/Reporting Container processes circulation insights and compliance audits within EU data residency boundaries.
• It provides secure, anonymized data access for Library Administrators and Compliance Officers.

## Key Elements
• Users: Library Administrators, Compliance Officers
• Containers: Analytics/Reporting Container (Kubernetes, EU-hosted), Self-Service Portal Container
• Databases/Storage: Dedicated read-replica database, Analytical data store, Ephemeral report storage
• Infrastructure/Tools: Apache Spark, dbt, Apache Kafka / AWS SQS, Prometheus

## Relationships
• Self-Service Portal Container -> Analytics/Reporting Container: Sends usage data via mTLS (Service Mesh / SPIFFE/SPIRE)
• Analytics/Reporting Container -> Read-Replica Database: Queries analytical data asynchronously
• Analytics/Reporting Container -> External Identity Provider: Authenticates via OAuth2/OIDC tokens

## Technology Stack
• Kubernetes: Orchestrates container workloads with strict ResourceQuotas and Horizontal Pod Autoscaling
• Apache Spark & dbt: Executes scheduled off-peak ETL pipelines and data transformations
• Kafka / SQS: Decouples asynchronous export generation and message queuing
• OAuth2/OIDC: Enforces Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Dynamic Row-Level Security (RLS)
• Customer-Managed Keys (CMK): Encrypts data-at-rest within EU regions

## Rationale
• Read-replica architecture and off-peak ETL processing isolate reporting workloads to prevent degradation of operational search performance.
• Data minimization, automated PII pseudonymization, and strict egress filtering guarantee compliance with EU data residency and GDPR mandates.
